newsitem.title: USA: Olympics organizers have no new bomb probe leads.
newsitem.headline: Olympics organizers have no new bomb probe leads.

text.p: Responding to an FBI plea for fresh leads to help the investigation into July's bomb blast at the Atlanta Olympic Games, organisers of the games said on Tuesday they had nothing left to give federal authorities.
The FBI said on Monday it would pay up to $500,000 for information leading to an arrest and conviction in the July 27 explosion, which caused two deaths and more than 100 injuries.
The Atlanta Committee for the Olympic Games (ACOG) said video tapes from security cameras at the park were turned over to investigators on the day of the bombing.
"That was in the hands of the FBI within hours," ACOG chief operating officer A.D. Frazier said. "Everything we've had has been turned over long since."

Olympic organisers have fully cooperated with the investigation but have not been briefed on it, ACOG president Billy Payne said. "We have not been a participant in the governmental investigation," he said.

The Atlanta Journal newspaper reported on Tuesday that the FBI had received more than 300 calls since offering the reward. The report quoted FBI spokesman Paul Bresson as saying he did not know how many of the calls were useful.
"Typically, when we set up a hotline, we get a lot of calls that don't have any investigative usefulness," he said.
